lemma: BOUNDARY-RANK LEMMA. G finite graph, no isolated vertex (else PM=0, count:=0). E = A disjoint-union B. D = vertices incident to both A and B. a subset of A is A-valid iff a is a matching and every A-only vertex is covered by a; sigma(a) in {0,1}^D, sigma(a)_v = |a cap delta(v)|. B-valid b, tau(b) symmetric. Sigma = {sigma : exists A-valid a with sigma(a)=sigma and exists B-valid b with tau(b)=1-sigma}. Claim: for every field F, rank_F M = |Sigma| for M[a,b] = PM(a u b). Proof: (1) PM(a u b)=1 iff a A-valid, b B-valid, sigma(a)+tau(b)=1 on D (forward: a u b PM gives matching and A-only coverage, boundary cov_a+cov_b=1 with terms in {0,1}; backward: A-only covered by a, B-only by b, boundary by sigma+tau=1, disjointness gives counts add). (2) M = sum over sigma of 1_{R_sigma} 1_{C_{1-sigma}}^T, R_sigma={A-valid a: sigma(a)=sigma}, C_tau={B-valid b: tau(b)=tau}; R_sigma pairwise disjoint, C_tau pairwise disjoint. (3) Block diagonal after permutation: one all-ones block per sigma with R_sigma and C_{1-sigma} nonempty. (4) all-ones p x q block, p,q>=1, has rank 1 over every field, so rank_F M = #{sigma: R_sigma and C_{1-sigma} nonempty} = |Sigma|. Corollary: rank_F M <= 2^{|D|}. Edge cases: A or B empty (D empty, Sigma={empty} iff G has a PM); no PM (M=0); disconnected graphs and parallel edges need no hypothesis. Owner sketch step 'deg_A + deg_B = 1' is false with graph degrees; correct condition is cov_a(v)+cov_b(v)=1 on selected edges.

proved_step: VTREE-EXISTENCE LEMMA (repair of the refuted all-vtree form). Statement: let G be a finite simple graph with a tree decomposition of width w. Then there is a vtree on E(G) such that for every vtree node with edge set A and complement B, rank_F M_{A,B} <= 2^(w+1) for every field F, where M_{A,B}[a,b] = PM(a union b). Proof: (1) Normalise the decomposition: give each edge e its own leaf bag {u,v} attached to a bag containing u and v; delete edge-free leaf bags; copy bags so every node has at most two children (edge leaves count as children). Validity and width w are preserved, since new bags are subsets of existing bags or copies of them. (2) Root the normalised tree T at r. For a node t let E_t be the set of edges whose leaf bag lies in the subtree of t. Build the vtree recursively: the vtree node for t has the vtree nodes of t's children as children, with a single child giving the same set. Every vtree node then has edge set E_t for some t. (3) For non-root t with parent p, the partition A = E_t, B = E minus E_t is induced by the tree edge tp, because subtree(t) is one component of T minus tp. By the tree-decomposition cut argument, every v in D(A,B) lies in X_t and X_p, so |D| <= w+1. By BOUNDARY-RANK LEMMA, rank_F M <= |Sigma| <= 2^|D| <= 2^(w+1). (4) Root node: B is empty, so rank <= 1. Corollary: the sweep bags of C_m x K_2 (width 5) give a vtree with all node ranks <= 64 over every field. Separately, the sweep step-boundary cuts have |D| <= 4 and rank <= 16 (S0003).

lemma: EXACT RANK IDENTITY (cut form of S0001). Setup: finite simple graph G=(V,E), edge partition E=A⊔B. D=V(A)∩V(B), Ao=V(A)\V(B), Bo=V(B)\V(A). Valid row a⊆A: a matching covering all of Ao. Valid column b⊆B: matching covering all of Bo. Signature σ(a)∈{0,1}^D, σ(a)_v = number of edges of a at v. M[a,b]=1 iff a∪b is a perfect matching of G. Claim: for every field F, rank_F M = |Σ|, where Σ = {σ(a): a valid, some valid b has σ(b)=1−σ(a)}. Proof: (i) For valid a,b: a∪b is a PM iff every v∈D has σ(a)_v+σ(b)_v=1 (vertices of Ao,Bo are covered exactly once automatically, since a and b are matchings and do not share vertices outside D). So M[a,b]=[σ(b)=1−σ(a)], and zero rows/columns for invalid a/b. (ii) Hence row a equals the indicator χ_{1−σ(a)} of the column set {b valid: σ(b)=1−σ(a)}. Distinct signatures give disjoint column supports, so the distinct nonzero rows have disjoint supports and are linearly independent over any F; all other rows are zero or repeat these. So rank_F M = |Σ|. Corollary: rank_F M ≤ 2^{|D|}, and rank is field-independent. Parity: 2|a| = |Ao| + Σ_v σ(a)_v, so |Ao|+|σ| is even on valid rows.

proved_step: LEMMA (parity coset, session R1229). Setup as S0001: G=(V,E) with no isolated vertices, E = A disjoint-union B, D = V(A) cap V(B), Ao = V(A)\V(B). For every valid row a (a matching in A covering all of Ao) with signature sigma(a) in {0,1}^D: |sigma(a)| (number of D-vertices covered by a) = |Ao| mod 2. Proof: every vertex of Ao has degree exactly 1 in a, and every vertex of D has degree sigma(a)_v in {0,1}; a uses no other vertices. So 2|a| = sum of degrees = |Ao| + |sigma(a)|, hence |sigma(a)| = |Ao| mod 2 (mod 2 reduction of 2|a| = |Ao| + |sigma(a)|). Consequence: Sigma is contained in the affine hyperplane {sigma in {0,1}^D : |sigma| = |Ao| mod 2}, so |Sigma| <= 2^(|D|-1) for D nonempty, and rank_F M <= 2^(|D|-1). Scope: any partition satisfying the no-isolated-vertices hypothesis. This is an UPPER bound and does NOT lower-bound |Sigma|; it is recorded as a bookkeeping fact, not as progress toward G0006.

proved_step: SWITCHING LOWER BOUND (CLAIMED, session R1237). Setting: finite simple graph G=(V,E) with no isolated vertices; E = A disjoint-union B; D = V(A) cap V(B) (assumed nonempty); Ao = V(A)\V(B); Bo = V(B)\V(A). Valid row a: a matching inside A covering Ao. Valid column b: a matching inside B covering Bo. sigma(a) in {0,1}^D is the indicator of vertices of D covered by a. Sigma = {sigma(a): a valid and some valid b has sigma(b) = 1 - sigma(a)}. Claim: if G has a perfect matching M0 and r pairwise vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles C_1..C_r exist, each containing a vertex v_i in D whose two C_i-edges lie on different sides of the partition, then |Sigma| >= 2^r (hence rank_F M_{A,B} >= 2^r for every field F, by the rank identity S0001). PROOF. Step 1 (every PM splits): for a PM M, put a = M cap A and b = M cap B. Each v in Ao has all its G-edges in A, so a covers Ao, and b covers Bo likewise. For v in D exactly one M-edge meets v, and it lies in A or in B, so sigma(b) = 1 - sigma(a) on D. Hence sigma(M cap A) in Sigma for every PM M. Step 2 (flips): for S subset of [r], M_S = M0 symmetric-difference (union of E(C_i), i in S) is a PM: each vertex of C_i has one M0-edge and one non-M0 cycle edge, and flipping swaps them; vertices off the cycles are untouched. Step 3 (independent bits): v_i lies only on C_i, so the M_S-edge at v_i is the M0-edge e_i^0 if i not in S, and the non-M0 cycle edge e_i^1 if i in S. These two edges lie on different sides, so sigma(M_S cap A)_{v_i} = c_i XOR [i in S], where c_i = [e_i^0 in A]. Hence S -> sigma(M_S cap A) is injective (S and S' differ at v_i for any i in the symmetric difference), and by Step 1 its image lies in Sigma. So |Sigma| >= 2^r. QED. Consistency: each crossing vertex is in D, and |D| >= 2r, compatible with the parity bound |Sigma| <= 2^(|D|-1) (S0011, SURVIVED_REVIEW). Scope: uses only PERFECT MATCHINGS (a function in P), so the perfect-matching control applies and the lemma transfers to no non-P function.

proved_step: CLAIMED (R1287, claude-haiku-5-5). Restatement of S0015 for arbitrary r. Setting: G bipartite with parts A and B; M0 a perfect matching; C_1..C_r pairwise vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles; for each i a D-vertex v_i on C_i whose two C_i-edges go to different sides (one in A, one in B). For S subset of [r] let M_S = M0 xor (union of E(C_i) for i in S). Claims: (i) M_S is a perfect matching; (ii) the side of v_i under M_S is the side under M0 flipped iff i in S; (iii) the 2^r matchings M_S have pairwise distinct signatures, so |Sigma| >= 2^r. Proof of (i): a vertex outside the union of the C_i keeps its M0 edge. A vertex u on C_i has exactly one M0 edge and one non-M0 edge inside C_i (alternation), and the flip exchanges them, so u stays matched exactly once; vertex-disjointness means no vertex is affected by two cycles. Proof of (ii): v_i's M0 partner lies across one of its two cycle edges; after the flip its partner lies across the other, which is on the opposite side; cycles C_j, j != i, do not touch v_i. Proof of (iii): by (ii), the bits at v_1..v_r of the signature determine S, so the map S -> signature is injective. Membership of each signature in Sigma follows from (i): the A-part of M_S covers A-side vertices and the B-part covers the B side, as in the finite check cm-f4bb37887d0c4b7d. Assumption carried over from S0015: the signature records the side of each D-vertex. Not re-verified in this turn: the exact definition of Sigma as written in Q-3376c4c863.
